creator: Alexander Terp
description:
No bridge that has ever died in the field has reached `Respawns::ended`. `a_2HrmSyRAQ` built the replacement policy and is marked done; the event that drives it does not arrive, so no pane has ever been replaced. Two runs on 0.4.1, two different ways for a bridge to die, zero respawn decisions in either.

**Run 44143, a refused attach.** Three bridges started against terminals an orphaned client still held:

    14:02:14.246  bridge.start          w4:p3  takeover=false
    14:02:14.251  pane.typeable         p2073ed9cw
    14:02:14.782  bridge.attach.failed  w4:p2  already has an attached client
    14:02:14.783  bridge.attach.failed  w4:p1
    14:02:14.783  bridge.attach.failed  w4:p3
    (nothing further)

**Run 56662, a settled bridge losing its connection.** Three bridges rendered steadily for fifteen minutes, then the network changed:

    14:13:53.643  bridge.frame.first    (x3)
    14:14:00 - 14:22:15   bridge.frames, continuously
    14:28:47.533  tunnel.down           (and flapping from here, see a_2IRdZK6Un)
    14:29:04.487  bridge.closed  w4:p3  herdr's stream ended without a closing frame  rendered=true
    14:29:04.489  bridge.closed  w4:p2  (same)
    14:29:04.491  bridge.closed  w4:p1  (same)
    (nothing further, for the two minutes to the end of the log)

The second is the exact case the policy exists for. `rendered=true` and fifteen minutes of life put it well past `SETTLED_NS`, so `ended` would have returned `Start(1)`, and a replacement carries `--takeover` because `bridgeRestarts > 0`. It never got asked.

## Where the chain stops

    libghostty close_surface callback
      -> rendererCloseSurface           Sources/MusterRenderer/Renderer.swift:61
      -> Surface.reportExit             Renderer.swift:279
      -> SurfaceView.paneEnded          SurfaceView.swift:144   logs pane.bridge.exited
      -> Core.bridgeExited              MusterWindow.swift:516
      -> session::bridge_exited         session.rs:1719
      -> Respawns::ended                session.rs:1759

`pane.bridge.exited` is absent from both run logs, and it is the first thing `paneEnded` does. So nothing after `rendererCloseSurface` ran, and the callback did not fire.

Leading hypothesis: libghostty is not closing the surface. Every dead pane sat on its own "Process exited. Press any key to close the terminal." screen, which is libghostty holding the surface open rather than asking the host to close it - and `close_surface` is the callback for the latter. The doc comment on `rendererCloseSurface` anticipates that screen and assumes the callback arrives anyway:

> a surface whose process ended keeps rendering the last thing it painted - libghostty's own "press any key to close the window" screen, among others - and nothing else in the app can tell that apart from a live pane

Unverified from here, and cheap to settle: with a pane in that state, press a key in it and watch for `pane.bridge.exited` in the run log. If it appears on the keypress, the callback is real and merely late by a human action, which is the same as never for this purpose.

## Why this is the one to fix

It recovers both failures on its own. The relaunch case in `a_2IQsToWVW` needs `--takeover`, and a working respawn supplies it without anybody relaxing the first-attach rule. The network-change case here needs nothing else at all.

It also means the corpus is passing on an event sequence the app never produces. `corpus/conformance/respawn.json` drives `ended` directly, so the policy is well covered and the wiring into it is not covered anywhere.

## Fixing it

- **Do not depend on `close_surface` for this.** The bridge is a process Muster spawned and can watch itself - its exit is observable without asking libghostty to volunteer it. That also decouples "the bridge died" from whatever libghostty decides to do with the surface.
- **Or make libghostty close the surface**, if a config setting governs the "press any key" screen. Cheaper if it exists; it changes what a genuinely dead pane looks like, which is a decision rather than a fix.

## Validating a fix

- Kill a bridge process by hand while its pane renders. `pane.bridge.exited` appears, followed by a respawn decision, and the pane comes back.
- Pull the network on a remote pane and restore it. The pane recovers without a relaunch, which is `a_2HrmSyRAQ`'s original claim and has never been true.
- A pane whose daemon is genuinely gone still gives up after `LIMIT` tries rather than spawning forever. That is what the policy is for and it has never been exercised in the app.
- An end-to-end case, not just a corpus one. The gap this card describes is precisely a policy that is tested and unreachable.
title: 🧟 No bridge that dies ever reaches the respawn policy, so no pane is ever replaced
